doc.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

title: Classical piano study in college
summary: She studied classical piano through college, playing Chopin, but knew she was more drawn to Ellington; she is nearing a milestone birthday.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I play some — I studied classical music. I was not a music major but I studied piano all through college. And my shining hour was, you know, a couple of Chopin etudes and scherzos and when I was in college, because the best thing that happened to me was a practice room in a building away from anything to distract me. And I can’t believe that I was able to practice and learn and memorize these things. But after that I really knew, and even my teacher knew that Beethoven, Bach and I were not wed and that I was much more into Ellington. But I still think it was the most important thing I could do and I loved playing them and I pull out a few things to do and the Gershwin preludes and now I’ve really gotten — I figure I can do this because you know there — I’m very sad about — well I’m nervous, in a few days I will turn a gulp — a really gulp age. I’m in good company because we baby boomers are very special, but nonetheless it is wigging me out.
